text.p: Precision Drilling Corp, which earlier launched a takeover bid for competing oil and gas driller Kenting Energy Services Inc, welcomed a possible merger between Kenting and Lynx Energy Services Corp, Precision chief executive Hank Swartout said on Monday.
"Actually, I like the Lynx deal," Swartout said in a phone interview. "It just makes it a lot easier because we would have had to take them next anyway."
Kenting and Lynx said they planned to merge drilling operations after Precision's offer was announced on Monday.
Precision said it planned a cash and stock takeover of Kenting, which was recently spun off from Trimac Ltd and whose shares had yet to be priced.
Swartout said he estimated the value of his firm's offer at about C$400 million. But the value price had to be boosted to account for Lynx, he said.
Precision already owns 15 percent of Lynx shares, making it the smaller drilling firm's largest single shareholder.
He said Kenting represented an attractive acquisition for Precision because it would take five to seven years to build the number of rigs that would come immediately with the deal.
"The boom is now, not later, and shareholder value is now, not later," he said.
If the deal was successful, Precision would operate 166 rigs in Canada, representing about 34 percent of the country's red-hot drilling industry.
The company also operates other oilfield service businesses including well servicing, compression equipment sales and service and oilfield equipment rentals.
Swartout said he spoke to Kenting executives on Sunday about his firm's planned advance and the news came as no surprise.
Precision's plans for Kenting had been widely rumored for some time in Canada's energy industry and financial markets.
"Everybody had talked about it," Swartout said. "He wanted to put his little surprise in but we knew that surprise was coming too, so that's why we all reacted at the same time."
Precision expects to mail its offer within the next 10 days.
Precision shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange soared 5.10 in Monday trade to 66, far above their 52-week high.
Lynx was up 2.60 to 14 in thin trade.
